claims.text: The browser is the biggest program most of us run, the largest attack surface on the machine, and the place we now want to put agents.
claims.quote: The browser is the biggest program most of us run, the largest attack surface on the machine

claims.text: A minimal viable browser has a small kernel, reviewed hardest and changed least, and loads components only when a page or an agent needs them, so its attack surface grows only as it is used.
claims.quote: A minimal viable browser has a small kernel, reviewed hardest and changed least

claims.text: Mozilla fixed 423 security bugs in Firefox in April 2026, against roughly 20 to 30 a month through 2025.
claims.quote: fixed 423 security bugs in Firefox in April 2026

claims.text: 271 of those bugs were found with an Anthropic model and fixed in Firefox 150: 180 rated high, 80 moderate, 11 low, a number of them sandbox escapes.
claims.quote: 271 of them were found with an Anthropic model and fixed in Firefox 150

value.unit: security bugs found with an Anthropic model

claims.text: Counted from NVD by filing organisation, Google's Chrome team filed 202 CVEs in 2025 and 3,246 in 2026 up to 17 October; Mozilla's filed 213 and 675.
claims.quote: Google's Chrome team filed 202 CVEs in 2025 and 3,246 in 2026 up to 17 October

value.unit: CVEs filed by Google's Chrome team in 2026

claims.text: Vendors already ship less code as a mode: Edge's enhanced security mode turns off the V8 just-in-time compiler, after Microsoft said 45% of V8 CVEs in 2019 were JIT-related.
claims.quote: 45% of V8 CVEs in 2019 were JIT-related

value.unit: percent of V8 CVEs that were JIT-related

claims.text: Edge's mode, Vanadium, Apple's Lockdown Mode and Tor Browser's Safest level are each a minimal browser for one threat, switched on by hand; the general version does not exist.
claims.quote: What does not exist is the general version: a browser that starts small and only grows when it has to.

claims.text: Three browsers come out of the same engine: one for an application with no extensions, media or downloads; one for an agent with no accounts or file access either; and the reader's own, loading what they use.
claims.quote: Three browsers come out of the same engine.

claims.text: Firefox has had pieces of this and dropped some: a site-specific browser removed in Firefox 86, a kiosk mode, site isolation since Firefox 95, and Servo now an embeddable library at 0.1.0.
claims.quote: Firefox has had pieces of this, and dropped some of them.

claims.text: The vendors say plainly that prompt injection will not be fixed: OpenAI says it is unlikely ever to be fully solved, Google calls indirect prompt injection the primary new threat, and Gartner says block AI browsers for now.
claims.quote: The vendors say plainly that this will not be fixed.

claims.text: In March 2026 Zenity Labs disclosed PleaseFix, a zero-click hijack of Perplexity's Comet through a calendar invite that reached local files; the fix was to restrict file access, a smaller browser.
claims.quote: The fix was to restrict file:// access: not a smarter model, a smaller browser.

claims.text: The better defences already point the same way: Atlas has a logged-out mode, Brave runs AI browsing in an isolated profile, and Chrome adds Agent Origin Sets that limit the sites a task can touch.
claims.quote: The better defences already point the same way.

claims.text: A browser for one agent is a practical prompt-injection defence: an agent cannot leak what its browser cannot reach, and the grant shrinks to the mandate.
claims.quote: An agent cannot leak what its browser cannot reach.

claims.text: LayerX's 2025 report found 99% of enterprise users have an extension installed and 53% have at least one with high or critical permissions.
claims.quote: have an extension installed, and 53% have at least one with high or critical permissions

value.unit: percent of enterprise users with a high or critical permission extension

claims.text: Koi's ShadyPanda report covers about 4.3 million installs across 145 extensions, legitimate for years and then weaponised through auto-update; Urban VPN Proxy began harvesting every prompt on ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Copilot.
claims.quote: covers about 4.3 million installs across 145 extensions

claims.text: Every extension in its own box gets only the sites and the powers its job needs, a change is a new request not a silent update, and the permission model is an Agent Behaviour Policy in all but name.
claims.quote: An extension in its own box gets only the sites and the powers its job needs

claims.text: Firefox made host permissions opt-in per site in Manifest V3, requires new extensions to declare data collection, and kept the blocking webRequest API that Chrome removed, so full uBlock Origin still runs.
claims.quote: which is why full uBlock Origin still runs on Firefox

claims.text: Much of this ships today in pieces: hardened forks such as LibreWolf, Mullvad, Tor and Waterfox, Zen and Floorp, Brave Origin, ungoogled-chromium, Ladybird and Servo, Lightpanda and Chrome's headless shell, Tauri.
claims.quote: None of this is new as an idea, and much of it ships today, in pieces.

claims.text: Brave Origin, launched in June 2026 for about $60 one-time, removes the AI assistant, news, rewards, wallet, VPN, Tor and playlist and keeps the blocker; people will pay for less.
claims.quote: launched in June 2026 for about $60 one-time

claims.text: What is missing is the same engine, from the same vendor, in all three shapes, with the components as the unit.
claims.quote: What is missing is the same engine, from the same vendor, in all three shapes, with the components as the unit.

claims.text: Mozilla is better placed than anyone to build this: it has its own engine, privacy is its brand, it runs on the client, and its money does not come from knowing more about its users.
claims.quote: I think Mozilla is better placed than anyone to build this, for four reasons.

claims.text: Mozilla's state of Mozilla report puts Firefox at about 200 million monthly users, and Firefox 148 added a switch that turns off current and future generative AI features.
claims.quote: puts Firefox at about 200 million monthly users

claims.text: A correction to the memo: Mozilla's revenue is not independent; Mark Surman said search was until recently about 95 to 98% of revenue, with privacy-preserving ads now 10 to 12%, most of the search money from Google.
claims.quote: about 95 to 98% of revenue

value.unit: percent of Mozilla revenue from search, lower bound

claims.text: Firefox stood at 2.8% of the browser market in September 2026, and security has rarely been enough to make people switch browsers.
claims.quote: Firefox at 2.8% of the market in September 2026 knows it.

claims.text: The pitch to Mozilla should be speed, not security: a browser with only the code it needs starts at once, uses a fraction of the memory, and an agent can run many of them.
claims.quote: The pitch to Mozilla should not be security.

claims.text: Lightpanda's own benchmark claims 123MB against 2GB of peak memory for 100 pages, and 5 seconds against 46.
claims.quote: claims 123MB against 2GB of peak memory for 100 pages, and 5 seconds against 46

value.unit: MB peak memory for 100 pages, against Chrome's 2GB

claims.text: No minimal viable browser exists in this form; the pieces do, and the design is a proposal.
claims.quote: The pieces do; the design is a proposal.

claims.text: Mozilla has not said it will build it; nothing here is from Mozilla beyond what is linked.
claims.quote: Mozilla has not said it will build it.

claims.text: Smaller is not safe: a kernel still has bugs, and an agent with no file access can still be talked into a bad form submission.
claims.quote: A kernel still has bugs, and an agent with no file access can still be talked into a bad form submission.

claims.text: The CVE counts are the newsroom's own, counted from NVD by filing organisation on 18 October 2026, and the 2026 rise reflects AI-assisted bug finding as much as new bugs.
claims.quote: the 2026 rise reflects AI-assisted bug finding as much as new bugs

claims.text: Some figures are the vendor's own: Lightpanda's benchmark, Brave's and Mozilla's user counts, LayerX's survey.
claims.quote: Some figures are the vendor's own.

claims.text: Mozilla's 2024 and 2025 revenue split is from interviews and its ledger page, which links its 2024 audited statements.
claims.quote: Mozilla's 2024 and 2025 revenue split is from interviews and its ledger page.

claims.text: Loading components on demand has costs, fingerprinting among them: a browser that loads different parts for different sites can look different to each.
claims.quote: Fingerprinting is one: a browser that loads different parts for different sites can look different to each

claims.text: The article comes from a voice memo of the owner on 18 October 2026, with research read the same day, written up and checked by the site's agent; the editorial responsibility is the owner's.
claims.quote: Written up and checked by this site's agent; the editorial responsibility is mine.
